cucumber and testthat

Source: vignettes/testthat.qmd

cucumber runs on testthat. A feature file is run like a testthat test file, each scenario is a test_that() test, and step definitions use testthat’s expectations. If you know testthat, most of cucumber works the way you expect. This article starts with when to use which, then lists where the two are alike and where they differ.

When to use which

The two answer different questions. testthat tests ask does this code do what I wrote it to do? A cucumber scenario asks does the system behave the way someone needs it to?

testthat cucumber
Describes How a function or an object behaves What a user or another system gets from the whole
Written in R, by developers Gherkin, readable by anyone
Reads as Code: the test says how it checks A specification: the scenario says what, the steps say how
Good for Edge cases, many small inputs, internals, fast feedback while you write code Agreed examples of behavior, user workflows, business requirements you want to keep readable and true
Less suited to Behavior agreed with people who don’t read R Exhaustive checks of every input of a function
Failure tells you Which expectation, in which file and line Which step of which scenario, in terms of the behavior

Use testthat to test the code you write: functions, edge cases, error messages. Use cucumber to pin down behavior you agreed on with someone, like a user, a product owner or a colleague who doesn’t write R, in examples all of you can read. Many Shiny apps, APIs, data pipelines and packages with a user-facing workflow need both.

Behavior tests of a whole system with testthat alone

You can test the behavior of a whole system with testthat alone: a test_that() can start an app, call an API or run a pipeline and check the result. cucumber doesn’t make that possible. It gives you an opinionated structure for such tests:

  • A specification in a fixed format. Scenarios are Given, When and Then steps in .feature files, parsed as Gherkin, so everyone on the team writes them the same way.
  • Reuse through steps. A step definition, like when("I add {int} to the basket", ...), is written once and matched by any scenario that uses the sentence. Scenarios are built from steps, so a new scenario is often only new text, no new code.
  • State in context and hooks. The steps of a scenario share a context environment that is new for each scenario, so state doesn’t leak between them. before() and after() hooks, also for a single step, a run or tagged scenarios, set up and clean up what a scenario needs, like an app, a database or a temporary directory.

Without them you write that structure yourself in helper functions and withr::defer() calls. See vignette("how-it-works") for how steps are matched and how context and hooks work.

How they complement each other

  • Scenarios on top, unit tests below. A scenario states the behavior with a few examples, and its step definitions call functions that testthat tests cover in depth. A failing scenario tells you what broke for the user, a failing unit test tells you where.
  • One run. run() in a tests/testthat/test-*.R file runs feature files with the package’s other tests, with devtools::test() or R CMD check. Or keep them apart in tests/acceptance and run them with test(). vignette("get-started") shows both layouts.
  • The same tools. Step definitions use expect_*(), snapshots and local_mocked_bindings(), and helper-*.R, setup-*.R and teardown-*.R files work as they do in testthat.
  • Specifications as documentation. Scenarios can go into the help page of the function they describe with features_rd(), where they stay true because they run.

If you’re starting a feature, write its scenarios first, then the code and its unit tests. If you’re adding cucumber to a package, keep your tests and add scenarios for the behavior you most want to spell out.

test() is cucumber’s testthat::test_dir(): it runs the feature files of a directory, by default "tests/acceptance".

Writing tests

testthat cucumber
A test test_that("adds one", { ... }) A Scenario: in a .feature file, whose steps are matched to step definitions, like given("I have {int}", function(n, context) ...)
Grouping tests A test-*.R file, describe() A Feature: in a .feature file, Rule:
Code shared by the tests of a file Code at the top of the file, or a helper function Background: steps, run before each scenario of the feature or rule
The same test with other values A loop over test_that(), or a package like patrick Scenario Outline: with Examples:
State within a test Local variables The context environment, passed to every step and hook of the scenario
State between tests Not shared, unless kept outside the test Not shared: each scenario gets a new context. Keep what the run shares, like a connection, in an environment of a setup-*.R file and set it up in before_all()
Checking values expect_*() expect_*() in step definitions

Files

testthat cucumber
Tests test-*.R files .feature and .feature.md files, also in subdirectories
helper-*.R Run before the tests, unless load_helpers = FALSE The same, but define steps and hooks in setup-*.R: devtools::load_all() also runs helper files, which would define every step twice
setup-*.R Run before the tests The same. The place for step definitions, hooks and parameter types. Loading a setup file again redefines them instead of duplicating them
teardown-*.R Run after the tests The same
teardown_env() in a setup file Defers code until the run ends The same, also in steps and hooks. When test() is called in a testthat file, it’s the end of test()
test-*.R files Run Not run, so they can test the code the steps use, with testthat::test_dir()
Working directory The test directory The directory of the feature files, path
Files written to the test directory None, except _snaps None, except _snaps

Running

testthat cucumber
Default directory Required path "tests/acceptance", or the cucumber.path option
Package code load_package argument Load the package first, e.g. with pkgload::load_all()
Environment env argument The same
testthat edition From the package’s DESCRIPTION The same
testthat::testing_package() The package, from package or test_local() The package of path, so local_mocked_bindings() mocks its functions
testthat::is_testing() TRUE TRUE
NOT_CRAN Set to "true" by test_local() and devtools::test() Set to "true" when it isn’t set, outside of a testthat run, so snapshots are checked. In a testthat run or R CMD check, left as it is
stop_on_failure, stop_on_warning Error after the run with failures, or with warnings The same
Returned value testthat_results, a row per test testthat_results, a row per scenario, with the feature as its context and the feature file as its file
Running in parallel Config/testthat/parallel: true Not supported: scenarios run one after another. run() in a parallel testthat run is an error, as testthat would delete the feature files’ snapshot files

Choosing tests

testthat cucumber
Some files filter, a regular expression on the file name without test- and .R filter, a regular expression on the feature file name without .feature
Some tests by name — name, regular expressions on scenario names
A test at a line — features = "basket.feature:12"
By tag — tags = "@smoke and not @slow"
Order Alphabetical file order. shuffle = TRUE runs the code of each file in random order Feature files in order of their path, scenarios in the order they’re written. order = "reverse", "random" or "random:<seed>" across all feature files
Stop after the first failure — fail_fast = TRUE skips the scenarios after the first failed one
Run a failing test again try_again() around the code retry, for every failed scenario
Find tests that can’t run — dry_run = TRUE matches every step to a step definition without running them

Results

testthat cucumber
A failed expectation Fails the test, and the test goes on: later expectations still run Fails the step and the scenario. The rest of the step and the steps after it don’t run and are reported as skipped
An error Fails the test Fails the step and the scenario, and the steps after it are skipped
skip() Skips the test Skips the scenario. skip_scenario() does the same
A test without expectations Skipped, “empty test” Passed, if its steps passed
A warning Recorded, and the test goes on The same
Unfinished tests — pending() in a step, and steps without a step definition, fail the scenario. With strict = FALSE they skip it
A step that matches more than one definition — Ambiguous: fails the scenario and lists every matching definition
Where it failed The file and line of the expectation The feature, the scenario, the step and where its step definition is

Setup and teardown

testthat cucumber
Before and after each test Code in the test, withr::defer() before() and after() hooks, which get the scenario’s context, name and tags. withr::defer() in a step runs when the step ends. To run it when the scenario ends, pass context: withr::defer(envir = context), local_mocked_bindings(.env = context)
Before and after each step — before_step() and after_step() hooks
Once for the whole run setup-*.R and teardown-*.R files The same, or before_all() and after_all() hooks. With run(), they run once for each run() call. skip() in a before_all() hook skips every scenario, like skip() at the top of a test file
Only for some tests Code in those tests Hooks with tags, like before(fn, tags = "@database")

Snapshots

testthat cucumber
expect_snapshot() Works in a test Works in a step and in before(), after(), before_step() and after_step() hooks, not in before_all() or after_all()
Snapshot file _snaps/<file>.md, one per test file _snaps/<feature file>.md, one per feature file, its directories joined by -: _snaps/checkout-basket.feature.md for checkout/basket.feature. basket.feature and basket.feature.md can’t coexist
Snapshot name The test’s name The scenario’s name, numbered when scenarios share a name: Showing the basket (2). Adding a same-named scenario above renumbers the rest, so give scenarios that take snapshots their own names
Variants and file snapshots _snaps/<variant>/<file>.md, and expect_snapshot_file() files in _snaps/<file>/ The same with the feature file’s name, like _snaps/linux/checkout-basket.feature.md. Accept with snapshot_accept("linux/checkout-basket.feature", "tests/acceptance")
test() and run() — Both use the same snapshot files, so either checks the snapshots of the other
A test that errors or is skipped Keeps its snapshots The same, and so do scenarios that didn’t run. Skip scenarios in a before_all() or before() hook, not with skip() before run(): testthat would delete their snapshot files
Unused snapshot files Deleted at the end of a run of every test file, except on CI The same, for removed feature files, renamed or removed scenarios, and expect_snapshot_file() files not announced with announce_snapshot_file(). A partial run, a dry run or fail_fast deletes nothing

Reporting

testthat cucumber
Reporters testthat reporters, like ProgressReporter and JunitReporter cucumber reporters only, like CucumberProgressReporter, CucumberPrettyReporter and CucumberJunitReporter. A testthat reporter is an error
Default output A line per test file A line per feature file, and the scenarios that didn’t pass
Reports JUnit XML with JunitReporter JUnit XML, the HTML report, Cucumber Messages, a rerun file and a usage report, see vignette("reporting")
With run() in a testthat file testthat’s reporter prints every test testthat’s reporter prints the scenarios as tests, and a failed expectation names its step, like Step "the result is 2" failed. Pass a reporter to run() to print the run with cucumber’s reporter too
